evidence.paraphrase: Gregg explains the properties of an acid strong enough to dissolve everything but gold, used to eliminate the body.
evidence.quote: The vat contained an acid powerful enough to destroy anything--except gold. In fact, the vat itself had to be lined with gold-leaf. I knew that in twenty-four hours there wouldn't be a recognizable body left, and in a week there wouldn't be anything at all.

evidence.paraphrase: The acid is described as dissolving tissue, bone, and ores, keeping them in suspension.
evidence.quote: The stuff utterly dissolves animal tissue, bone, even the common ores--keeps them in suspension.

evidence.paraphrase: Gregg frames what he witnessed as contradicting known natural laws.
evidence.quote: It is a physiological absurdity--it contradicts the laws of natural science.

evidence.paraphrase: Gregg describes observing a reverse of decomposition occurring in the vat.
evidence.quote: For hours at a time I've watched the change.... Did you ever see a body decompose? Of course not! Neither have I. But you must know in a general way what the process is. Well, this has been the exact opposite!

evidence.paraphrase: The dissolved remains reform into a skeleton.
evidence.quote: First, I stared at the heap of grave-mold as it shaped itself into _bones_, a skeleton.

evidence.paraphrase: Hair and flesh regenerate on the reforming body as Gregg watches.
evidence.quote: I watched the coming of hair, a yellow tangle of it sprouting from the bare round skull, until--oh, God!--the flesh began making itself before my eyes!

evidence.paraphrase: The body progressively returns to life, showing color, open eyes, and breathing.
evidence.quote: I've watched her limbs grow rosy! Her lips are scarlet! Her eyes are bright--they opened yesterday--and her breasts were rising and falling--oh, almost imperceptibly--but that was last night.

evidence.paraphrase: Terrified of the reviving body emerging, Gregg refuses to remain.
evidence.quote:
Soon she's going to get out of that vat!_" Gregg bleated.
"Jeannette, forgive me--God, forgive me--but I will not--I cannot--I dare not stay here to see her then!

evidence.paraphrase: Gregg repeatedly returns to observe and test whether what he saw was real.
evidence.quote: I replaced the lid. I spent a week convincing myself that it was all impossible, that I _couldn't_ have seen anything of the sort. Then I went to the vat again----

evidence.paraphrase: Gregg cocks a revolver, leading to his suicide.
evidence.quote: The loud click was the cocking of the revolver.

evidence.paraphrase: The ending reveals Gregg had been blind for years, undercutting the reliability of what he described seeing.
evidence.quote: Asa Gregg was blind ... had been, since that night three years past when the acid splashed....

evidence.paraphrase: The watchman is frightened by recurring groaning sounds in the building.
evidence.quote: Every night lately he heard the same peculiar noise somewhere in this wing of the building.... Like a body groaning and turning in restless sleep, it was. It scared him.
